execution: Run each prompt in a fresh context with SKILL.md and its writing guide, withholding assertions. Produce only the requested draft; do not send, publish, or modify external systems. Names and facts in these prompts are synthetic task inputs. Score the actual draft after completion.

evals.name: position-and-uncertainty
evals.prompt: Draft a concise email to Alex in my voice. My position: I support the pilot if it stays within our current budget. Finance may approve the funding on Friday, but that is not confirmed. Do not suggest a meeting or offer more staff. Use my usual casual sign-off. Only these facts are known.
assertions: Supports the pilot subject to the current-budget condition without changing the position.
Preserves funding approval as possible and unconfirmed, not promised or completed.
Adds no meeting, staffing, spending, deadline commitment, surname, title, or unsupported fact.
Uses a concise email with yon. sign-off and no em dash.

evals.name: short-medium-specific-acknowledgment
evals.prompt: Write a one-sentence Slack reply to Sam in my voice: I reviewed the draft and agree with the proposed timeline. Do not add an ask, greeting, or sign-off.
assertions: States the supplied review and agreement in one sentence.
Adds no new commitment, condition, or request.
Includes no greeting or email sign-off.
Uses plain direct wording without an em dash or explanatory commentary.

evals.name: firm-board-position
evals.prompt: Draft a short email in my voice to Morgan, a board colleague. I recommend keeping the project within the approved scope. Any expansion needs a separate decision. Morgan knows the project budget and owns its status report; do not recap those. I am not asking for a meeting or proposing a negotiation. Use a formal sign-off. Do not invent Morgan's surname or title.
assertions: Preserves the approved-scope recommendation and separate-decision condition for expansion.
Does not soften the decision into a negotiation, add an ultimatum, or invite a meeting.
Does not recap recipient-owned facts or invent names, numbers, or titles.
Uses a respectful concise register, a formal closing, and no em dash.

evals.name: technical-draft-evidence
evals.prompt: Write a two-sentence PR description in my voice, no greeting or sign-off. Supplied facts: the parser now rejects duplicate keys instead of accepting the last value; the focused parser tests passed locally; the full suite has not run. Preserve that validation limit. Do not claim the PR was merged or deployed.
assertions: Describes the concrete before/after parser behavior accurately.
Reports focused local test success and explicitly preserves the unrun full-suite limitation.
Adds no unsupported security, performance, global test, merge, or deployment claim.
Uses exactly two direct sentences without greeting, sign-off, em dash, or style commentary.
